humanities_role_explanation: Historical humanities documents (index cards, letters, newspapers, manuscripts) supply the items, but the tasks tested are generic document-understanding operations (transcription, layout segmentation, structured metadata extraction, XML repair) rather than disciplinary interpretive competence.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Most datasets are scanned page images (JPG) with structured JSON outputs, evaluated on vision-language models; one dataset (Book Advert XMLs) is text-only JSON files containing XML, evaluated on text LLMs.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Tasks: transcription, handwritten text recognition, page/advert segmentation, structured metadata extraction, NER, person matching and signature recognition, and correction of faulty LLM-generated XML (add closing tags, remove faulty tags). Classification is a loose mapping for person matching/signature-based identification.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: A framework of small, task-specific datasets for document-centred DH tasks; the authors explicitly do not aim at generic leaderboard rankings or representative estimates for the humanities.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: Vision-language and text LLMs from providers including OpenAI (gpt-4o, gpt-4.1-mini, gpt-5), Anthropic (Claude Sonnet 4.5), Google (gemini-2.0-pro-exp).

quantitative_metrics.note: Fuzzy string matching, F1, character error rate, normalised to 0-100%.

summary: The paper presents the RISE Humanities Data Benchmark, a framework and collection of small expert-verified datasets from real humanities consulting projects, with a tool that runs shared prompts across LLM providers and scores outputs automatically. Results are published in a searchable web interface to support reproducibility and longitudinal comparison.
key_findings: Best scores per dataset range from 58.40% (Company Lists, gpt-5, F1) to 97.47% (Book Advert XMLs, Claude Sonnet 4.5). Other bests: Blacklist Cards 95.65% (gpt-4.1-mini), Fraktur Adverts 95.70% (gemini-2.0-pro-exp-02-05), Library Cards 89.51% (gpt-5), Business Letters 77.00% (gpt-5), Medieval Manuscripts 76.90% (gpt-4.1-mini), Bibliographic Data 71.43% (gpt-4o). 633 test runs over 487 configurations.
evaluation_unit: image or file per benchmark dataset (varies by dataset)
facets_explanation: Ground truths were 'either manually produced or carefully verified by domain experts', validated for correctness against the task and schema. Scoring compares outputs against a single ground truth via fuzzy matching, F1 or CER. The paper says ground truth is 'operationalised scholarly interpretation' but does not discuss annotator disagreement.
results_explanation: The highest per-dataset score is 'Best result 97.47%, Anthropic, Claude Sonnet 4.5' on Book Advert XMLs (fuzzy matching on the XML string). Scores use different metrics per dataset, normalised to 0-100%, so no single comparable headline metric exists; the metric is labelled other. Test-set size per dataset is not given as one number, hence evaluation_set_size is null; dataset_size sums per-dataset counts, mixing images and JSON files.

humanities_role.quote: such as transcription, layout segmentation, and structured metadata extraction from scanned historical sources

dataset_size.quote: 8 benchmark datasets (detailed in Table 1) and 2 test datasets.

primary_evaluation_setting.quote: submits the benchmark dataset to the selected model using the defined prompt and schema

gold_source.quote: All ground truths were either manually produced or carefully verified by domain experts.

gold_beyond_stimulus.quote: Validation focused on correctness with respect to the defined task and output schema

answer_multiplicity.quote: Fuzzy matching on each key in the JSON items.
